title: Ordinary connected-component lower bound near the generic point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of schemes [def-pc-scheme], where $S$ is nonempty and irreducible (any two nonempty open subsets intersect) with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and suppose the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_\eta$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has exactly $n$ connected components, where a connected component is a maximal nonempty connected subset [def-weil-connected-scheme]. There exists an open subset $W\subseteq|S|$ containing $\eta$ such that, for every $s\in W$, the ordinary residue-field fibre $X_s$ has at least $n$ distinct connected components. The empty generic fibre and $n=0$ are allowed. No field extension is made in this conclusion, and no Noetherian, flatness, finite-presentation or separatedness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: If $n=0$, take $W=|S|$: every fibre has at least zero components. Suppose $n>0$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], identify $|X_\eta|$ with $F=f^{-1}(\{\eta\})\subseteq|X|$. Enumerate its components as $A_1,\ldots,A_n$. The maximality assertion of [lem-sfb-connected-component-maximality] shows that every point lies in one of these components and that two different components are disjoint: the union of two connected sets meeting at a point is connected, since a separation would put both sets on the side containing that point. Each $A_i$ is closed in $F$. Indeed, its closure in $F$ is connected: a separation of that closure into two relatively clopen sets restricts to a separation of $A_i$, so $A_i$ lies on one side, and density forces the other side empty. Maximality then identifies this closure with $A_i$. Put $C_i=\overline{A_i}^{\,|X|}$. Closure in a subspace gives $C_i\cap F=A_i$. Thus the $C_i$ are closed, their union contains $F$, and $(C_i\cap C_j)\cap F=\varnothing$ for $i\ne j$.

proof.text:
Let $C= igcup_{i=1}^n C_i$, a closed subset because the union is finite. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-fibre-closed-cover-spread] to $g=f$, $y=\eta$, and the two closed subsets $C$ and $\varnothing$. Its hypotheses hold because $f$ is locally of finite type and quasi-compact, and $F\subseteq C\cup\varnothing$ by Step 1. Since $\overline{\{\eta\}}=|S|$, it gives an open $W_0
i\eta$ with $f^{-1}(W_0)\subseteq C$. For each distinct pair $i,j$, apply [lem-sbc-generic-fibre-closed-avoidance] to $f$, $\eta$, and the closed subset $C_i\cap C_j$, whose intersection with $F$ is empty by Step 1. It gives an open $W_{ij}
i\eta$ on whose inverse image $C_i\cap C_j$ is empty. Intersect $W_0$ with these finitely many opens, obtaining $W_1
i\eta$. On every fibre over $W_1$ the traces of the $C_i$ form a pairwise disjoint finite closed cover.

proof.text: For each $i$, the closed subset $C_i$ meets $F$, since it contains the nonempty component $A_i$. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-closed-subset-fibre-nonempty] with $h=f$, $T=S$, its generic point $\eta$, and $C=C_i$. It supplies an open $V_i\ni\eta$ such that $C_i\cap f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is nonempty for every $s\in V_i$. Set $W=W_1\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^n V_i$. This is open and contains $\eta$. For every $s\in W$, the sets $B_i=C_i\cap f^{-1}(\{s\})$ are nonempty and form a pairwise disjoint finite closed cover of $f^{-1}(\{s\})$. This is precisely the generic-flatness and open-image part of Stacks 055D packaged in the cited closed-subset nonemptiness lemma; its statement explicitly imposes no Noetherian, reducedness or separatedness hypothesis.

proof.text: Fix $s\in W$. Each $B_i$ is also open in the topological fibre, since its complement is the finite union of the other closed $B_j$. Choose $b_i\in B_i$ and let $D_i$ be its connected component supplied by [lem-sfb-connected-component-maximality]. A connected subset meeting both $B_i$ and its complement would be separated by these clopen sets. Therefore $D_i\subseteq B_i$. The $D_i$ are pairwise distinct, since they contain their respective $b_i$ and the $B_i$ are disjoint. This exhibits $n$ distinct connected components. The homeomorphism of [def-pc-scheme-fibre] transports them to components of the ordinary scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$, proving the conclusion without a field extension.
